research.title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Languages of India need 1.6 to 14 times as many tokens as English on GPT-4o's tokenizer for the same content, which makes them more expensive and slower to serve. We train tokenizers from scratch on human-written. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Commercial language model APIs bill per token, so a tokenizer that needs more tokens for the same content in one language makes that language more expensive, slower, and able to fit less text in a fixed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Assisted history matching remains non-unique because many geological realisations can reproduce equivalent production responses with substantial differences between individual well matches. This ambiguity increases when a field comprises several depositional settings and modelling strategies. The paper. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmark scores for medical large language models (LLMs) are difficult to interpret when scoring criteria cannot be traced to clinical evidence. Here we developed Med Evidence Bench (MEB, https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/), comprising 1,536 physician-constructed items across three levels. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: RLVR trains language models to reason by rewarding correct final answers. A widely used algorithm, group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), gives every token of a solution the same credit, so dense process rewards have been proposed to. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable potential in biomedical applications, while agentic memory systems have emerged as a promising approach to preserving and utilizing information across tasks and interactions. However, a fundamental question remains: how. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
